thread.title: FAANG Stocks Fall As Concerns About Growth Continue| Investor's Business Daily

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: FAANG Stocks Fall As Concerns About Growth Continue| Investor's Business Daily
text:
All five of the FAANG stocks were smacked Monday on a down day in the stock market, as analysts remain concerned about a weakening outlook and other troubles for the technology giants.
X
The FAANG stocks — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOGL ) — have long been industry darlings, representing the biggest stocks in tech and the internet.
One of the most troubled was Facebook stock. It plunged 5.7% to close at 131.55 on the stock market today . Facebook stock is down 40% since hitting a record high of 218.62 on July 25.
On Monday, the Wall Street Journal reported that Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg placed the blame for privacy failures that rocked the company earlier this year on Sheryl Sandberg, the company's chief operating officer. The WSJ report fueled flames stoked by an explosive New York Times investigation published last week. That story revealed how the social media behemoth handled the spread of disinformation as well as mishandling data privacy and security issues.

How Amazon, Apple Fell Meanwhile, Amazon stock dropped 5.1% to 1,512.29. It's down 26% off its high set on Sept. 4. Amazon reported third-quarter results on Oct. 25 that fell short on revenue and gave a weak fourth-quarter revenue forecast. Its core e-commerce business showed decelerating growth for a second quarter.
Apple stock fell 4% to 185.86, as a steady drumbeat of negative reports about iPhone demand and production cuts continues to pressure Apple stock. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday that Apple has slashed production orders for all three of the iPhone models it unveiled in September.
Apple stock is down 20% from its high of 233.47 set on Oct. 3.
Rival Concerns Hit Netflix, Google Further, Netflix stock dropped 5.5% to close at 270.60, falling 36% from its high of 423.20 set on June 21. Competitive concerns have pounded Netflix stock recently.
Shares of Google-owner Alphabet closed at 1,027.42, down 3.8%.
The company reported third-quarter results on Oct. 25 that missed revenue estimates . Rising competition with Amazon is a concern.
